full_judgment: 6. The learned Advocate has next argued that since the learned Magistrate had directed all concerned to be informed about shifting of the date, this official act must be deemed to, have been regularly performed. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has relied on the decision in the case of Srinivas Mall Bairoliya and another Vs. Emperor in A.I.R. 1947 P.C. 135 (136) In the said case their Lordships of the Privy Council while considering whether the Price Control Order was duly promulgated held that it would be legitimate to presume under section 114 of the Evidence Act that it had been duly promulgated but such a presumption might easily be rebutted. In the said case, their Lordships also had evidence by which the presumption instead of being, rebutted was further strengthened. The facts of the present case, I find are clearing distinguishable from the facts of the case relied on by the learned Advocate. In the instant case, the learned Magistrate merely passed an order on an off date to inform all concerned. But there is neither and evidence or any finding that 'all concerned; were ever informed of the learned Magistrate's order The contention of the learned Advocate in this regard is also without any substance.
